- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 7 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after rising) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model often fails to correct; adjust downward by 1–2% for next 5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates in high-sentiment periods; apply 2–4% downward bias if sentiment > 0.75 over last 5 days.  
- If sentiment flips from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
